italian.name: Deutz Gambit
italian.summary: Use rapid development to support d4; the Deutz pawn offer trades material for open lines.

italian.name: Giuoco Pianissimo, Canal Variation
italian.summary: Pin the f6 knight before deciding whether to open the center with d4.

italian.name: Hungarian Defense, Tartakower Variation
italian.summary: Against the Hungarian setup, central space matters more than a quick attack on f7.

italian.name: Evans Gambit, Anderssen Variation
italian.summary: When the Evans bishop retreats to e7, recover central space with d4 before launching an attack.

italian.name: Evans Gambit, Harding Variation
italian.summary: Block the check with Bd2 in this Evans branch; compare piece activity before recovering material.

italian.name: Evans Gambit, Lasker Defense
italian.summary: The Lasker defense returns material to simplify. Keep development ahead of pawn hunting.

italian.name: Classical Variation, Center Holding Variation
italian.summary: Keep the central pawn tension while completing development; d4 is a plan, not an obligation.

italian.name: Classical Variation, Closed Variation
italian.summary: The closed Italian delays exchanges so both sides can finish development before choosing a pawn break.

italian.name: Classical Variation, Greco Gambit, Greco Variation
italian.summary: The Greco gambit opens the center before castling. Watch checks and the safety of the e4 pawn.

italian.name: Classical Variation, Greco Gambit, Modern Line
italian.summary: This modern central line emphasizes active development rather than trying to preserve every pawn.

italian.name: Classical Variation, with d5
italian.summary: When Black challenges with d5, resolve the central tension before starting a flank attack.

italian.name: Scotch Gambit, Max Lange Attack
italian.summary: The Max Lange attack involves forcing central exchanges; calculate checks before grabbing material.

italian.name: Two Knights Defense, Fried Liver Attack
italian.summary: The Fried Liver sacrifice forces the king toward the center. Calculate the forcing continuation rather than assuming a winning attack.

italian.name: Two Knights Defense, Fritz Variation
italian.summary: The Fritz knight jump changes the attack on f7 into a fight for central tempi.

italian.name: Two Knights Defense, Lolli Attack
italian.summary: The Lolli plan prepares an attack with d4 before committing to a sacrifice on f7.

italian.name: Two Knights Defense, Ulvestad Variation
italian.summary: The Ulvestad counterattack uses b5 to deflect the bishop. Check captures and threats before retreating.

sicilian.name: Smith-Morra Gambit Accepted, Classical Formation
sicilian.summary: Against the Morra gambit, accept only with a clear development plan; White gains open files for the pawn.

sicilian.name: Alapin Variation, Barmen Defense, Central Exchange
sicilian.summary: Challenge the Alapin center with d5, then develop quickly rather than spending tempi with the queen.

sicilian.name: Alapin Variation, Stoltz Attack, Ivanchuk Line
sicilian.summary: White supports e5 in the Alapin; undermine the pawn chain and watch the bishop diagonal toward f7.

sicilian.name: Closed, Botvinnik Defense, Edge Variation
sicilian.summary: The Botvinnik setup controls d4 with pawns; develop the knight via e7 without obstructing the g7 bishop.

sicilian.name: Nyezhmetdinov-Rossolimo Attack, Gurgenidze Variation
sicilian.summary: The Rossolimo trades early bishop activity for pressure on your queenside. Counter in the center before chasing the bishop.

sicilian.name: Accelerated Dragon, Maróczy Bind, Gurgenidze Variation
sicilian.summary: Against the Maroczy Bind, exchange a pair of knights and seek a well-prepared d5 or b5 break.

sicilian.name: Taimanov Variation, Bastrikov Variation
sicilian.summary: The Taimanov queen on c7 supports e5 and leaves the dark-squared bishop several development squares.

sicilian.name: Scheveningen Variation, Keres Attack
sicilian.summary: Against the Keres pawn advance, keep king safety central to your calculation; do not respond automatically with more pawn moves.

ruy.name: Steinitz Defense, Nimzowitsch Attack
ruy.summary: Challenge the Steinitz structure with d4 while using the bishop to influence the center.

ruy.name: Schliemann Defense, Classical Variation
ruy.summary: The Schliemann creates immediate central tactics. Resolve checks and captures before returning to quiet development.

ruy.name: Berlin Defense, Anti-Berlin Variation, Anderssen Variation
ruy.summary: The Anti-Berlin keeps queens on and supports e4 with d3 before changing the pawn structure.

ruy.name: Berlin Defense, Berlin Wall
ruy.summary: In the Berlin endgame, weigh the bishop pair against White’s healthier pawn majority; king activity becomes important.

ruy.name: Exchange Variation, Alekhine Variation
ruy.summary: After the Exchange variation removes queens, use the central knight and pawn majority rather than look for a quick attack.

ruy.name: Open, Berger Variation
ruy.summary: In the Open Spanish, challenge Black’s central pawns and use development to recover the pawn.

ruy.name: Marshall Attack
ruy.summary: The Marshall break d5 offers a pawn for activity. Decide whether to accept only after considering king safety.

ruy.name: Closed, Breyer Defense
ruy.summary: The Breyer reroutes the knight to d7. Use the extra time to build a central plan instead of chasing it.

queens-gambit.name: Central Variation, Rubinstein Defense, Yefimov Gambit
queens-gambit.summary: In the sharp accepted center, White takes space while Black tries to hold c4; calculate the pawn race before advancing further.

queens-gambit.name: Classical Defense
queens-gambit.summary: Recover the gambit pawn through development with Bxc4; Black’s c5 challenges your center immediately.

queens-gambit.name: Exchange Variation
queens-gambit.summary: The exchange creates a Carlsbad pawn structure. Plan a minority attack or a central e4 break after development.

queens-gambit.name: Tarrasch Defense, Pseudo-Tarrasch Bishop Attack
queens-gambit.summary: The Tarrasch structure may leave an isolated pawn. Develop actively and decide whether to blockade or exchange it.

queens-gambit.name: Semi-Tarrasch Defense
queens-gambit.summary: The Semi-Tarrasch challenges d4 with pieces and pawns; clarify the central exchanges before choosing a plan.

queens-gambit.name: Vienna Variation
queens-gambit.summary: The Vienna check changes the move order. Meet the immediate check before continuing normal development.

queens-gambit.name: Tartakower Defense
queens-gambit.summary: The Tartakower prepares a queenside fianchetto. White can maintain the center and choose when to exchange on d5.

queens-gambit.name: Orthodox Defense, Main Line
queens-gambit.summary: In the Orthodox setup, Rc1 increases pressure along the c-file while both sides prepare central exchanges.

caro-kann.name: Two Knights Attack, Mindeno Variation, Retreat Line
caro-kann.summary: In the Two Knights, the bishop retreats to h5 to retain the pin; watch g4 ideas before committing the king.

caro-kann.name: Advance, Short Variation
caro-kann.summary: The Short setup develops calmly behind e5. Challenge the pawn chain with c5 once your pieces support it.

caro-kann.name: Exchange Variation, Rubinstein Variation
caro-kann.summary: In the Exchange structure, activate both bishops and contest the open central files.

caro-kann.name: Panov Attack, Modern Defense, Carlsbad Line
caro-kann.summary: The Panov gives White an active isolated-pawn setup. Develop and pressure d4 rather than chase pawns.

caro-kann.name: Panov Attack, Modern Defense, Czerniak Line
caro-kann.summary: The queen sortie to a5 adds pressure on c3. Check tactical replies before taking a second pawn.

caro-kann.name: Breyer Variation, Stein Attack
caro-kann.summary: The Breyer delays d4. Use the extra time to build central control while keeping the light-squared bishop active.

caro-kann.name: Endgame Variation
caro-kann.summary: With queens exchanged, develop the king and minor pieces; the lost castling right is less important in an endgame.

caro-kann.name: Advance Variation, Van der Wiel Attack, Dreyev Defense
caro-kann.summary: Qb6 pressures b2 and d4 in the Advance. Balance those targets against the need to complete development.

kings-indian.name: Semi-Classical Variation, Exchange Variation
kings-indian.summary: When White exchanges on e5, recapture centrally and use the open files rather than force a kingside pawn storm.

kings-indian.name: Fianchetto Variation, Panno Variation, Blockade Line
kings-indian.summary: Against the fianchetto, block the center with e5 and coordinate the queenside pieces before choosing a pawn break.

kings-indian.name: Fianchetto Variation, Yugoslav Variation, Exchange Line
kings-indian.summary: After White exchanges on c5, use the open d-file and the central pawn structure to organize counterplay.

kings-indian.name: Averbakh Variation, Benoni Defense, Advance Variation
kings-indian.summary: The Averbakh restricts your kingside development; c5 challenges White’s center and can lead to Benoni structures.

kings-indian.name: Four Pawns Attack, Normal Attack
kings-indian.summary: Challenge the Four Pawns center with c5 and e6; attack its base rather than allow every pawn to advance freely.

kings-indian.name: Sämisch Variation, Byrne Defense
kings-indian.summary: The Byrne setup prepares queenside expansion against the Samisch. Keep an eye on White’s possible long castling.

kings-indian.name: Sämisch Variation, Panno Main Line
kings-indian.summary: The Panno prepares b5 with a6 and Rb8. Check how White’s center responds before opening the queenside.

kings-indian.name: Petrosian Variation, Stein Defense
kings-indian.summary: Against the Petrosian center, a5 restrains b4. Coordinate your pieces before preparing the f5 break.

french.name: Exchange Variation, Bogoljubow Variation
french.summary: The Exchange opens the c8 bishop. Develop actively and avoid assuming that symmetrical pawns require a draw.

french.name: Advance Variation, Milner-Barry Gambit, Main Line
french.summary: The Milner-Barry gambit offers a central pawn for development; finish development before trying to keep extra material.

french.name: Tarrasch Variation, Guimard Defense, Main Line
french.summary: The Guimard develops the knight before the c-pawn. Support central pressure without trapping the c8 bishop.

french.name: Tarrasch Variation, Open System, Main Line
french.summary: The open Tarrasch trades central pawns. Use piece activity and watch the pressure on the isolated d-pawn.

french.name: Rubinstein Variation, Fort Knox Variation
french.summary: The Fort Knox reroutes the light-squared bishop via d7 to c6; accept less space in return for a solid structure.

french.name: McCutcheon Variation, Lasker Variation
french.summary: The McCutcheon counter-pin creates tactical exchanges. Calculate checks before changing the central pawn chain.

french.name: Classical Variation, Burn Variation, Main Line
french.summary: The Burn exchanges the e4 pawn and develops into a solid center. Contest the open files after castling.

french.name: Winawer Variation, Poisoned Pawn Variation Declined
french.summary: In the Winawer, White declines the poisoned pawn and develops Bd3. Keep central pressure rather than rely on a queen raid.

london.name: Early c5 and Qb6
london.summary: Meet pressure on b2 with Qb3; if Black gains space with c4, keep the queen safe before developing.

london.name: Bishop exchange on d6
london.summary: Exchanging on d6 removes Black’s active bishop. Use c4 to contest the center rather than play a fixed setup.

london.name: Early queen check
london.summary: The b2 pawn can be offered for development, but calculate the queen’s escape squares before committing to this sharp line.

london.name: Against a kingside fianchetto
london.summary: Complete development against the fianchetto and keep d4 supported; choose a central break before a wing attack.

london.name: Against the Dutch setup
london.summary: Give the bishop a retreat square and watch the e5 break against Black’s Dutch structure.

london.name: Against the early e5 break
london.summary: Central exchanges can expose a tactic on e5. Count defenders before assuming that a London formation must stay closed.

london.name: Queenside fianchetto
london.summary: Against a queenside fianchetto, c4 contests d5 and uses the extra space without exposing your king.

london.name: Jobava development
london.summary: The Jobava move order creates early threats on c7; retreat when Black meets them and return to development.
